:::{#rem-criteria-training-error}
#### Criteria that adjust the training error

@def-adjusted-r-squared, @def-mallows-cp, @def-aic and @def-bic each correct a fit measure computed on the [training set](#def-training-set) for the number of parameters.
They need no [held-out set](#def-held-out-set), so they cost one fit per model, where [cross-validation](#def-kfold) costs several.

For a least squares model with Gaussian [noise](#def-noise) of known [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance), $-2 \llikf{\est{\vparam}}$ equals $\text{RSS}(\est{\vparam}) / \varpar$ plus a constant that does not depend on the model.
AIC then equals $\nobs C_p / \varpar$ plus a constant, so the two criteria rank models the same way.

Each criterion assumes a [model family](#def-model-family) whose parameter count measures its [flexibility](#def-flexibility).
When the noise variance is [estimated](estimation.qmd#def-estimate) from the [fitted model](#def-fitted-model) itself, the estimate can reach zero, and the criteria then fail.
Cross-validation makes no such assumption.

:::
